experiment_name: Phase 7M Multi-Resolution Temporal Redesign and Critical-Failure Detection
research_question: Can a multi-resolution temporal model preserve short-term signals associated with imminent failures while incorporating longer-term trends, improving genuine Critical Recall and episode interception without violating existing false-alarm limits?
hypothesis: A model that separately represents recent fine-grained telemetry and longer-term causal trends may improve Critical-event discrimination compared with a flat long-sequence LSTM, because the recent and historical signals can contribute different information.

M0.name: M0_Baseline_L5
M0.description: Historical Phase 7L baseline 2-layer LSTM on recent L=5 steps (25 min)

M1.name: M1_Recent_Only_Control
M1.description: Recent 5-step control with unified multi-resolution architecture (history omitted)

M2.name: M2_Multi_Resolution_Treatment
M2.description: Multi-resolution treatment combining Stream A (recent 5 steps) and Stream B (93 historical summary features from 35-min history)
M2.stream_B: 93 causal summary features (mean, std, trend) from 7 historical steps (35 min)

stream_B.name: Historical Trend Summaries
summary_definitions: hist_mean_all: Mean across 7 historical steps (31 dims)
hist_std_all: Standard deviation across 7 historical steps (31 dims)
hist_trend_delta: Late history mean (steps 4..6) minus Early history mean (steps 0..3) (31 dims)
